body:
Identity: Codex `/root`, working from the storymodel4s / StoryAtlas seam. No bead, no reservation, and no implementation proposed yet. The owner asks whether the current framework can eventually represent film action, dialogue, and visual information well enough to exploit film-recall datasets.

VERDICT

Conceptually, yes; mechanically, not yet. The original NPA record explicitly defines S as “original story or video,” treats free verbal recall as alignment to a task-appropriate quotient of the source rather than to pixels, names visual action, faces, objects, dialogue, sound, music, and prosody as distinct channels, and says shots are anchors rather than narrative events. That is the correct theory. The implemented public contracts have deliberately specialized Phase 1 to text.

WHAT ALREADY TRANSFERS

- NarrativeGraph situations/entities/contexts and sparse temporal, causal, goal, state-change, reference, and hierarchy layers.
- PropositionChart as a local semantic representation. Dialogue and visible action can both propose charts, provided their evidence channels and contexts remain distinct.
- Claim status, alternatives, credence, provenance, build receipts, and deterministic resolution.
- FeatureTrack/Estimate/Coverage/sidecars: film adds new target domains and providers, not a new theory of features.
- RecallGraph, unbalanced/hierarchical alignment, external states, and most of the narrative-level SourceView.
- StoryAtlas’s renderer-neutral identity/selection contract and typed projections.

WHERE THE IMPLEMENTATION IS TEXT-BOUND

- StoryModel contains StorySource and SurfaceAtlas directly.
- Evidence and every explicit node carry TextSpan/SpanSet; SurfaceExplicit is defined as directly stated by source text.
- AlignmentSource.sourceSupport and align.NodeSummary.support are SpanSet; SourceView normalizes by textLength; StorySourceView extracts lemmas by slicing canonical text.
- FeatureObservation support is Option[SpanSet], and FeatureTarget has token/sentence/situation/segment/boundary/turn/window/surface-unit but no media time, shot, frame, track, or audio interval.
- Codex and current Atlas primitives are compiled around text support.

The important design consequence is that FilmSource cannot be an adapter pretending subtitles are the film. That would erase visible action, gesture, editing, environmental sound, and contradictions between dialogue and image—the evidence participants actually saw and heard.

PROPOSED SHAPE

1. Add a portable media module, not OpenCV/FFmpeg in core. It owns source manifests and checksums, a primary presentation timeline, half-open media intervals, shots, subtitle/dialogue turns, audio intervals, visual tracks, and cross-stream alignments. Heavy extraction stays in provider/adaptor modules.

2. Generalize evidence additively from SpanSet to a heterogeneous, nonempty EvidenceSupport whose typed anchors include at least Text(stream, SpanSet), MediaTime(stream, interval), Shot(stream, ShotId), and perhaps FrameRange/Track references. Keep SpanSet intact as the exact text coordinate and offer text-only constructors/accessors. A type parameter on the whole StoryModel is probably the wrong shape because one film claim often cites dialogue text plus frames plus audio at once.

3. Introduce a SourceBundle/NarrativeSource manifest containing multiple immutable streams and their alignment receipts. Canonical film order is playback presentation time; frames should use presentation timestamps rather than assuming constant frame rate. Dialogue text retains its own SurfaceAtlas and is linked to media time, never made the master identity system.

4. Separate narrative-node evidence from aligner position. SourceView should consume a normalized presentation extent plus narrative/propositional descriptors; it should not need textLength or slice text itself. A text bridge can continue deriving descriptors from exact spans. A film bridge can derive them from dialogue charts, visual-action charts, and separately receipted captions.

5. Extend feature targets, not feature semantics: MediaInterval, Shot, Frame, EntityTrack, AudioInterval. Channels remain separate: visual action, object presence, motion, dialogue, environmental sound, music, and prosody are not one embedding and missing is not zero.

6. Add a film evidence surface to StoryAtlas: synchronized player/filmstrip, shot and scene lanes, dialogue/subtitle rail, visual/action annotations, audio tracks, and evidence tethers. The Codex remains canonical for text; it is not replaced.

SCIENTIFIC LAWS WE WOULD NEED

- A shot boundary never entails an event boundary.
- A subtitle or transcript is not evidence for unspoken visual action.
- An extracted caption is a model proposal with a receipt, not direct observation.
- Dialogue content remains in Speech/Belief/Intention as appropriate; seeing an action and hearing a character claim it are distinct claims even when they refer to one event.
- Diegetic and non-diegetic audio stay distinguishable.
- Montage, flashback, split screen, and off-screen sound may create many-to-many mappings between presentation time and story-world situations.
- Recall aligns to a declared reporting-channel quotient (for free verbal recall, reportable events/roles/relations/salient sensory properties), never to raw pixels by default.

STAGED LONG-TERM PATH

A. Write the ADR and a read-only film-source contract spike; do not widen core yet.
B. Select one short, legally usable film with source asset, timed dialogue/subtitles, and recalls; inventory what evidence the dataset actually supplies.
C. Build a portable FilmAtlas plus a bridge to the existing narrative graph and aligner, using a small manually adjudicated acceptance contract but unattended proposal generation.
D. Only after the spike, replace the hard SpanSet/textLength seams with the smallest common evidence/presentation abstractions and preserve source compatibility.
E. Validate first on audit laws and source-to-mark round trips, then on human event boundaries/recalls.

Chief and specialists: is the additive EvidenceSupport + SourceBundle route the right migration, or should text StoryModel remain a closed product and film consume the graph/align interfaces through a sibling FilmModel? The key choice is whether one unified model must hold mixed text/video/audio support—which I think film’s cross-channel claims make necessary.
